sources.entry: NVIDIA Grace Performance Tuning Guide - States the coherency fabric, LPDDR5X fit and MPAM cache and memory partitioning on Grace.

summary.title: Grace Performance Tuning Guide
summary.one_liner: NVIDIA's Grace CPU architecture reference covering its Neoverse V2 cores, Scalable Coherency Fabric, LPDDR5X memory, MPAM partitioning, NVLink-C2C and SVE2/atomics details relevant to tuning.
takeaways: Grace has 72 Neoverse V2 cores per CPU, with the Superchip giving 144 cores and up to 960GB LPDDR5X.
The Scalable Coherency Fabric is a mesh with distributed cache, providing over 3.2 TB/s bisection bandwidth; MPAM lets it partition cache, I/O and memory bandwidth.
Grace has two NUMA nodes per Superchip, and NVLink-C2C links CPU and GPU memory in Grace Hopper and Grace Blackwell systems.
Use LSE atomics rather than Load/Store Exclusives, which the page says do not guarantee forward progress in large systems.
Binaries built for Armv8 up to 8.5-A run on Grace, but NVIDIA HPC compilers produce code that is not binary compatible with Graviton.
summary.summary: The guide introduces NVIDIA's Grace CPU and its CPU Superchip, C1 and Grace Hopper/Blackwell variants, with spec tables for cores, cache, LPDDR5X capacity and bandwidth, and NVLink-C2C. It then explains the architecture: the Scalable Coherency Fabric mesh, MPAM-based cache and bandwidth partitioning, the LPDDR5X memory subsystem with ECC, PCIe Gen 5 I/O, and Neoverse V2 core support for SVE2, NEON, LSE atomics and Armv9 features. It is mostly architectural description rather than step-by-step tuning, and it points to other NVIDIA guides for Hopper and Blackwell tuning and to compiler docs for flags.
